_what:
toprow_profiles.py — the member-selection stage's profile on the TOP ROW of ALL 77
members. A DIAGNOSTIC (measurement only): nothing here builds, gates or changes a
product; the stage (run_member_crop.sh / member_profile.py) is untouched and its
centre-row default unchanged. Record: toprow_profiles.json beside this file; scratch
(Siril lists, .ssf) under datasets/corpus/qa_work/toprow_work/ (gitignored).

WHY A SIBLING OF row_profiles.py: that driver hard-codes its eight members and runs the
bottom row and the outer station too; this one runs ONE row on every member with the
identical method — the member's own CACHED centre-row station x-boxes (clamps included)
moved to the top row (box y 0..800), r 400, top-30, the recipe's constants, the rule
applied per row exactly as on the centre row (member_profile.apply_rule, imported).
Centre-row values are READ FROM THE CACHE (datasets/corpus/member_selection/profiles.json)
and never re-profiled; the cache's content premise is MEASURED here by re-hashing every
member before the first Siril run.

WHAT IT ANSWERS (ledger id toprow_profile_all77): whether the top-row softness the six
row-profiled members showed (+0.36..+0.50 px at the centre station, SYMMETRIC entry vs
exit — the case the asymmetry rule is blind to by design) is night-dependent across the
whole corpus, and the top-row frame score S_top for a corpus-relative row-level rule's
pre-registration (reported, not scored).

Every pixel op and every star is Siril's (load, crop, findstar via star_stations.measure);
the top-30 arithmetic is member_profile.py's own (imported). In-house: box placement and
bookkeeping. Removal condition: a tool reporting a headless row-resolved star-shape map
(the star_stations.py row of the register) retires this with row_profiles.py.
instrument: Siril findstar via star_stations.measure (gate 'setfindstar reset -roundness=0.05 -sigma=0.5 -relax=on'; load + crop + findstar -out per station); top-30-by-amplitude median of (FWHMx+FWHMy)/2 and of min/max roundness = member_profile.py profile()'s arithmetic (read_rows/apply_rule imported); centre-row values from the tracked cache, not re-profiled

P4_S_top.definition: mean of the top-row top-30 FWHM over {centre, exit -600..-2400} (member_profile.apply_rule S_advisory on the top-row stations)

verdict.P1: HELD 33/34 (97 %): the soft members' top-row centre station reads +0.27..+0.51 px over the centre row (aug14 set medians +0.35/+0.40/+0.41/+0.44/+0.39; aug09 set-04/05 +0.34/+0.38); the one miss aug14/set-01 at +0.273
verdict.P2: FAILED 8/30 (27 %): the CONTROLS' top rows are softer too — july31 set medians +0.09 / +0.23 / +0.29 / +0.37, aug06 +0.23 / +0.24 / +0.29 (min +0.045, max +0.393). The two pilot controls (+0.045, +0.185) were the two BEST cases (july31/set-01, the sharpest set, and aug06/set-01). The top-row softening is CORPUS-WIDE — every night, every set — a vertical off-axis term of the lens (the top-row boxes sit ~1576 px above the centre row), with the soft nights ~0.1..0.2 px worse than the controls at the centre station
verdict.P3: FAILED 7/34 (21 %) as operationalised (|entry − exit| ≤ 0.10 at BOTH ±1200 and ±1800): at ±1200 the top row IS near-symmetric on the soft sets (medians 0.01..0.13) but at ±1800 it diverges (0.08..0.32) — the top row carries the SAME entry-side asymmetry the centre row carries (top-row asym(2400) set medians: soft +0.16..+0.45, controls −0.10..+0.14; the bar would crop 29 members on the top row vs the stage's 27 on the centre row). The pilot's 'symmetric' was a statement about the centre-STATION softening being additive on both sides, which holds (P1) — not about entry equalling exit at the outer stations, which does not. So the top row carries TWO terms: a uniform additive softening on every night (corpus-wide) plus the night-dependent entry-side asymmetry the stage already removes on the centre row
verdict.P4: S_top p25 2.618 px; 29 of 77 exceed p25 + 0.20 = 2.818: aug14 set-02..05 (all 20 members, 2.86..3.15), aug09 set-04 (4 of 5: sub_02..05, 2.83..2.86), aug09 set-05 (all 4, 2.88..2.92), aug09/set-03/sub_05 (2.820 — on the bar); aug14/set-01 (2.78 median) and every july31/aug06 member (2.54..2.77) are under. The night gap roughly doubles from the centre row to the top row: S medians soft 2.78..3.09 vs control 2.54..2.77 at the top (gap ~0.4..0.5) against 2.50..2.74 vs 2.41..2.51 at the centre (gap ~0.2..0.25)
verdict.comparability: top-row / centre-row star counts per station: ratio median 0.94 (0.70..1.27 over 693 stations) — the top-30-by-amplitude populations are comparable in size
verdict.cache_premise_measured: 77/77 members re-hashed equal to the cache before the first Siril run
verdict.reading_for_U5: a corpus-relative ROW-level exclusion (S_top > p25 + 0.20, the frame rule's analogue on the top row) would remove the top 800 rows of exactly the soft nights' members (29: aug14 set-02..05, aug09 set-04/05, + one on the bar) — a night-quality exclusion again, but with a top-row gap (~0.4..0.5 px) about twice the centre-row gap that made the frame rule a NULL (~0.2..0.3). The uniform corpus-wide part of the top-row softening (every night +0.1..+0.4) is NOT removable by any exclusion — it is the lens's vertical radial term, present on every member (the same class as the symmetric horizontal softening selection cannot touch). Before U5 pre-registers a corner gain, the coverage of the canonical's bottom-left corner boxes by MEMBER (which nights' top rows feed corner_700_4200 / corner_1300_4900, from the compose gate record or a header-only WCS pin) decides whether excluding the 29 members' top rows starves those boxes or leaves control-night coverage — the rowmin dilution hypothesis, still uncounted
premises_not_tested: the row -> corner pin: 8 members pinned (rowmin Part A), 69 assumed by the same WCS geometry
the top-row softening is optical (field curvature / vertical off-axis term), not a registration or group artefact — single-raw top-row stations would test it
S_top's p25 + 0.20 as a threshold is the frame rule's constant carried over; its placement in the S_top continuum is not examined here (the same continuum question §4 raises for the 0.20 bar)
